editorial:
The Navigator is a 1924 American silent comedy directed by Donald Crisp and Buster Keaton, with Keaton and Kathryn McGuire as two sheltered people adrift on an abandoned ocean liner. The Internet Archive record calls it the most financially successful of Keaton's feature-length studio productions. Duke's Center for the Study of the Public Domain lists it among the films that entered the US public domain on January 1, 2020, so the 1924 print is free to reuse.

The rights trap is the copy, not the film. The Internet Archive copy carries Portuguese subtitles, and a modern copy may add its own music or other new material. Those additions can be protected even though the 1924 images are not. Use a clean copy and check what was added to it. The story, trademark and restoration layers are not yet researched.
faq: Can I reuse footage from The Navigator in my own video?
Yes for the 1924 images. The print is in the US public domain. Check whether your copy has a modern score or added subtitles, and take only the film itself.
Can I use the music that plays on a copy I found online?
Not automatically. The film is silent, so any music on a modern copy is a separate recording or composition. Use music you have cleared, or music that is itself public domain.
